title: Lifecycle Growth Sprint — Retargeting Creative Brief (LinkedIn + Google) — v0.9
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Lifecycle Growth Sprint: Retargeting Creative Brief (LinkedIn + Google)
Owners: Growth (Ben), PMM (Soojin), Mops (Tyler)
Date: Jan 2025

Slide 2 — What we’re trying to accomplish
Goal: lift activation (first successful production-like inference call) + early retention (repeat usage W1–2) for PLG/self-serve developers.
Retargeting role: bring back devs who signed up but didn’t activate, plus recently lapsed users.
Definition of “activation” for measurement: first_request_success (2xx completion) within 72h of click (primary). Secondary: first_streaming_success; dashboard_viewed (cost/latency).

Slide 3 — Who this is for (target segments)
Segment A: New signups who did NOT activate
- Signed up in last 1–14 days
- No “first_request_success” event
- May or may not have created an API key

Segment B: Partial activators
- api_key_created but no first_request_success
- Or first_request_success but no first_streaming_success (we can message streaming as “next step”)

Segment C: Recently lapsed
- Previously activated (at least one successful request)
- No usage in last 7–21 days (exact window per Tyler based on data volume)
- Exclude current high-intent sales-assisted (opportunity stage) unless Sales asks us to include in a separate play

Segment D (optional / later): Content-engaged non-signups
- Visitors to Quickstart/benchmarks pages but no sign-up
- NOTE: not part of initial sprint scope unless tracking is already robust

Slide 4 — Audience sources + rules (implementation notes)
Primary: first-party retargeting lists from product + marketing site
- Product events captured server-side + console (see ENG-2844)
- Landing page visitors via site pixel

Exclusions / suppression
- Suppress unsubscribed users (email opt-out) from retargeting where applicable (coordinate with compliance + Mops)
- Suppress existing active users with recent usage (avoid annoyance / wasted spend)
- Suppress internal employees, vendors, and known test accounts

Geos: NA + EU priority; APAC allowed if we can support regional routing/capacity without issues
Devices: desktop priority (dev workflow), mobile allowed for LinkedIn but expect lower activation conversion

Slide 5 — Key message pillars (developer-first)
Pillar 1: “Get to first success fast”
- Copy/paste curl + minimal SDK snippet
- Clear API key steps + predictable errors

Pillar 2: “Production inference economics you can control”
- Lower latency + lower cost via batching/caching/quantization (no hard promises)
- Show cost/latency breakdown in Console

Pillar 3: “Reliable paths to production”
- Hosted → Dedicated → Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Same API + operational tooling

What we should NOT do
- Don’t over-promise “fastest” or “cheapest” unless we link substantiation
- Don’t imply we host a proprietary model; we’re the inference platform
- Don’t use fear language about competitors

Slide 6 — Proof points we can safely use (and how)
Allowed with link:
- “Redwood-verified performance profiles” (link: docs/benchmarks page)
- “Streaming, function/tool calling, structured output support” (link: API docs)
- “Token-level latency/cost breakdowns in Console” (link: Console screenshots / docs)

Avoid / needs substantiation review (Ethan + Soojin)
- Any % improvements (e.g., “40% lower cost”) unless we cite a public blog/benchmark and specify conditions
- Claims about specific competitor performance

Slide 7 — Creative constraints (channel + brand)
Tone
- Developer-first, direct, no marketing fluff
- Prefer specific actions: “Run your first request in 2 minutes” (only if we can back it up with quickstart)

Channel constraints
LinkedIn:
- Static image + short headline; optional short video (<= 15s) if we can produce quickly
- Avoid dense code screenshots that won’t be legible on feed
Google:
- Responsive display: keep text minimal; rely on headline/description variants
- Search (optional): keywords around “LLM inference API”, “open model hosting”, “GPU inference”, “streaming chat API”

Visual constraints
- Follow Redwood brand: high contrast, clean, minimal
- Use product UI crops sparingly; highlight a single UI moment (latency/cost breakdown OR checklist)

Legal/privacy constraints
- No use of personal data in ad copy (“We saw you didn’t…”) — keep it generic
- No sensitive targeting categories

Slide 8 — Creative concept set (v1)
Concept 1: “First success” (new non-activated)
Headline options:
- “Make your first LLM request succeed.”
- “Your API key → first response. Fast.”
Body options:
- “Copy/paste quickstart + streaming example. See latency + cost per request.”
CTA: “Finish setup” / “Run quickstart”
Visual: simple diagram (API key → request → streaming response) OR single UI crop of “First request succeeded” state

Concept 2: “Streaming next step” (partial activators)
Headline options:
- “Try streaming responses in minutes.”
- “Lower perceived latency with streaming.”
Body options:
- “Enable streaming + see token latency in Console.”
CTA: “Enable streaming”
Visual: streaming UI representation (animated dots) + small “token latency” snippet (not too technical)

Concept 3: “Benchmarks + economics” (lapsed)
Headline options:
- “Predictable inference performance.”
- “Control cost per token.”
Body options:
- “Benchmark-backed profiles + batching/caching levers built in.”
CTA: “See quickstart” / “See benchmarks”
Visual: lightweight chart (latency distribution) + “Cost breakdown” UI crop

Concept 4: “Deployment flexibility” (enterprise-leaning lapsed)
Headline options:
- “Hosted today. VPC when you need it.”
Body options:
- “Same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.”
CTA: “Explore deployments”
Note: keep this as secondary; sprint goal is activation, not sales pipeline

Slide 9 — Copy blocks (approved language draft)
Short headlines (<= 30 chars-ish for testing)
- “Finish your first request”
- “Run the quickstart”
- “Try streaming responses”
- “See latency + cost”

Short descriptions
- “Copy/paste a working request. Then verify latency + cost in Console.”
- “Troubleshoot auth + model selection fast. Get to first success.”
- “Enable streaming and monitor token latency in minutes.”

CTAs
- “Run quickstart”
- “Finish setup”
- “View guide”
- “Open Console”

Slide 10 — Landing page expectations (variant for retargeting)
We will send retargeting traffic to a dedicated, activation-focused page (not the generic homepage).
Page must include:
1) Above the fold: single promise + 1 CTA
- Promise: “Get to first success” (not “buy now”)
- CTA: “Run quickstart” (links to code + console)

2) Quickstart flow (3–5 steps)
- Create API key
- Copy/paste curl (and optional TS/Python snippet)
- Confirm first 2xx response
- Optional: enable streaming
- Optional: view latency/cost dashboard

3) Troubleshooting section (prominent)
- Auth errors / permissions
- 401/403 guidance, missing env var, wrong base URL, model name confusion
- Link to Support if blocked (but we should try to unblock self-serve first)

4) Lightweight proof
- Link to benchmarks / “Redwood-verified performance profiles”
- 1–2 short bullets on reliability + deployment flexibility

5) Deep links
- Console: API keys page, “Create first request” page
- Docs: Quickstart, streaming, SDK minimal example

Slide 11 — Conversion expectations + page hygiene
Expectations
- Landing page loads fast (guardrail: don’t degrade perf, avoid heavy embeds)
- Works for logged-out and logged-in states
- If user is already logged in, send them directly to the relevant console step

Edge cases
- If user already activated: show “next step” version (streaming + dashboard)
- If user’s email is suppressed/unsubscribed: ads still okay, but ensure we’re not using messaging that implies email subscription

Slide 12 — Measurement plan (what success looks like)
Primary success metric (retargeting): activation rate within 72h of ad click
- Join: ad_click → utm captured → product events (first_request_success)
Secondary metrics
- CTR by concept + channel
- Landing page conversion rate (CTA click to quickstart/console)
- Time-to-first-success from click
- D7 repeat usage among activated-from-retargeting cohort
Efficiency metrics
- Cost per activated developer (CPAD)
- Cost per landing-page CTA click

Attribution approach (Tyler)
- UTMs required on every ad URL
- Capture UTMs into session + pass into event properties (ENG-2844)
- Use last non-direct click as default; also report view-through separately (do not mix)

Slide 13 — UTMs + naming conventions (v1 proposal)
Base
- utm_source: linkedin | google
- utm_medium: paid_social | display | search
- utm_campaign: lifecycle_sprint_wk1_retgt (update weekly)
- utm_content: concept1_firstsuccess | concept2_streaming | concept3_econ | concept4_flex
- utm_term: for search keywords only

Ad group naming (human readable)
- RETGT_A_nonactivated_1-14d
- RETGT_B_key_no_success
- RETGT_C_lapsed_7-21d

Slide 14 — Experiment design (what we’re testing)
Hypothesis
- Dev-specific “first success” creative + troubleshooting-forward landing page increases activation vs generic product messaging.

Test plan
- Test concepts 1–3 in parallel per segment
- Keep landing page constant for week 1; iterate in week 2 if we see clear drop-off points

Holdouts
- If feasible, maintain a small audience holdout (5–10%) for incrementality read (Tyler to confirm feasibility in platforms)

Guardrails
- Ad frequency cap to avoid spam perception
- Watch support ticket volume and “confused by ad” inbound (Avery/CS feedback loop)

Slide 15 — Operational checklist (pre-launch)
Creative
- Final copy approval: Soojin + Ben
- Benchmark/proof review: Ethan
- Design QA: Tessa/Kenji

Tracking
- UTM QA + event property validation: Tyler + Eng (ENG-2844)
- Confirm key events firing: api_key_created, first_request_success, first_streaming_success, dashboard_viewed

Suppression
- Ensure suppression lists are applied (unsubscribed + internal)

Links
- Validate all ad links and deep links (avoid 404s / console routing changes)

Slide 16 — Draft budget + pacing (placeholder)
Week 1
- LinkedIn: $X/day (heavier on Segment A)
- Google Display: $Y/day (Segment A + C)
- Optional Search: small budget for high-intent keywords if we can staff quickly

Week 2
- Reallocate to best-performing concept by CPAD (not CTR)

Notes
- We will likely see higher CTR for “benchmarks” and higher activation for “first success.” Optimize for activation.

Slide 17 — Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we include Segment D (content-engaged non-signups) in sprint scope, or defer?
2) What is the exact lapsed window (7–21d vs 14–30d) based on volume + behavior?
3) Are we comfortable using “in minutes” language, or keep it softer (“quickstart”) to avoid claim risk?
4) Final landing page owner + build approach (GTM web vs product docs)?

Slide 18 — Next steps + owners
By EOW (pre-launch)
- Creative v1 ready (Soojin/Tessa)
- Audience builds + suppression verified (Tyler)
- Landing page variant shipped + QA (Ben + Web/DevEx)
- Tracking QA + dashboard ready (Tyler + Mei + Sana)

During sprint
- Twice-weekly check: CTR/CVR/CPAD + qualitative feedback from Support/Sales
- Iterate creatives (2–3 variants) without changing measurement definitions midstream

Appendix — Notes to self (working)
- Keep at least one concept that leads directly into Console checklist step, not just docs.
- Add a troubleshooting-forward creative variant if we see high click / low activation (signal: users still hitting auth/model selection friction).
- If LinkedIn quality is low (high CTR, low activation), shift budget to Google where “dev intent” may be higher.
